history.dynasty: Modern temple -- built by local trusts with Rajasthani and Gujarati artisans
history.period: Opened to devotees in 2007 per a Wanderlog listing; one travel directory (Adequate Travel) claims an original 1963 temple built by Late Shri Ramanlal Maneklal Patel / founded by Maharani Padmavati Baiji -- uncorroborated and conflicting (verify)
history.summary: The Ahmedabad Vaishno Devi Temple is a modern replica of the Trikuta-mountain shrine of Jammu and Kashmir, standing on the Sarkhej-Gandhinagar (SG) Highway at the Vaishno Devi Circle landmark, near Nirma Institute. A 50-foot artificial hill of yellow sandstone simulates the Trikuta terrain, and devotees crawl through narrow artificial rocky caves to reach the sanctum with the three pindis; the complex includes a 1,350-square-foot multi-level hall said to hold up to 5,000 pilgrims at peak times and a small Bhairav Nath shrine. IDENTITY NOTE: the CSV's generic 'Vaishno Devi Temple, Ahmedabad' is documented here as the well-known SG Highway replica (street-level geocode match at Vaishno Devi Circle). The 1963 founding claim and 9 km-from-station details in one directory appear to describe a different or earlier city shrine and could not be corroborated -- flagged as uncertain.

name: Vaishnodevi Tirth Dham Mandir
town_description: Ahmedabad, on the banks of the Sabarmati, is Gujarat's largest city, founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmad Shah I. Its historic walled old city is a UNESCO World Heritage site, and it remains a major centre of textiles, commerce and education.
tradition: Shaktism (replica shrine of the Jammu and Kashmir original)

travel.airport: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad (verify distance).
travel.railway: Ahmedabad Junction (Kalupur) -- the temple is well outside the centre on the SG Highway (verify distance).
travel.road: On the Sarkhej-Gandhinagar (SG) Highway at Vaishno Devi Circle, Khoraj Cross Road area; the great majority of visitors arrive by car.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri is the most vibrant but most crowded period.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Conflicting reports: Justdial says 6:00 AM-7:00 PM daily; Wanderlog says premises open noon-6 PM; TripHobo says 6:00 AM-9:00 PM -- verify before visiting.
